newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 1997 car demand seen flat - JAMA.
newsitem.headline: Japan 1997 car demand seen flat - JAMA.

text.p: Japan's domestic vehicle demand in calendar 1997 will remain flat from 1996, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA) said on Thursday.
JAMA also estimated domestic vehicle sales in 1996, including 660 cc minivehicles, at 7.02 million vehicles, up 2.3 percent from the year earlier.

JAMA said sales in January to March 1997 are likely to increase by 100,000 units but then fall by the same amount in the April-June period, reflecting next April's planned hike in the consumption tax.
"Domestic car sales have not seen a full-fledged recovery yet because of poor demand for sedan models," Yoshifumi Tsuji, JAMA chariman, told a news conference.

"The car industry needs to reinvigorate the domestic market because Japan's car exports are expected to fall in the future in line with a planned increase in output at Japanese producers' overseas units," he said.
